newsitem.title: USA: Cosby testifies to affair, contact with accused woman.
newsitem.headline: Cosby testifies to affair, contact with accused woman.

text.p: Entertainer Bill Cosby testified on Tuesday that more than 20 years ago he had sex once with the mother of the woman who claims to be his daughter and who is on trial for attempting to extort $40 million from him.

Cosby, often stern in his delivery, told a Manhattan Federal Court jury that he agreed to help the woman and her daughter financially -- some $100,000 just since 1994 -- but had been constantly pressed by them for more.
Although actual paternity is not at issue in the trial, it emerged that Cosby had suggested taking a paternity test but then changed his mind because he feared disclosure in the media.

The television star, comedian and author has previously admitted to having an affair with Shawn Thompson, mother of 22-year-old Autumn Jackson, but he has steadfastly denied being the father of Jackson. She is one of 300 students whose education Cosby says he helped pay for through a foundation he established with Camille Cosby, his wife of 33 years.

He said that he had met Jackson at least twice and spoken with her on the telephone several times, at one time telling her: "Look Autumn, I'm not your father. I will be for you a father figure. I am open 24 hours a day. Let me know what you need."
In some 2-1/2 hours of testimony, Cosby said his contact with her was neither more nor less than that with other students he assisted.
Jackson was charged with trying to extort money from Cosby in return for not telling a supermarket tabloid newspaper that she is his illegitimate daughter.

Cosby testified that in his last conversation with Jackson in Dec. 1996 he told her: "I said to her that I was upset and I said 'I'm tired of you, I'm tired of your mother. You and your mother have never given me a happy moment for what I have given you.'"
Under questioning from government prosecutor Lewis Liman, Cosby recalled the affair and regular contact with Thompson, who called frequently to ask for money.
"I met her in the early 70s in a hotel in Los Angeles," said Cosby. "I asked her to dance and we did. And then I asked her for her phone number because I wanted to see her."
He said he contacted her and paid for her to fly to Las Vegas to visit him. Asked whether he had sex with her, Cosby said, "Yes."
Liman also asked Cosby how many times he had sex with her and he said, "I remember once."

Jackson was arrested in January. She and her alleged accomplices, Jose Medina, 51, and Boris Sabas, were charged with conspiracy, extortion and engaging in interstate commerce to commit crimes. If convicted they could face prison terms of 12 years and fines of $750,000.

The extortion plot came at a tragic time for the Cosby family. The entertainer's only son, Ennis, 27, was shot to death in California on Jan. 16, two days before Jackson was charged. Authorities have said the incidents are unrelated.
When the trial began last week, the government introduced a Jan. 16 letter Jackson wrote to former CBS President Peter Lund.

In the letter, Jackson said she wanted to speak to Lund and Cosby about her "undeserved and impoverished financial and living conditions" or she would expose the entertainer in a move that could hurt the ratings of his current CBS television programme. She said if Lund and Cosby could not help her, she would sell her story to the Globe supermarket tabloid.
